column1: #notes label(office_room_v2_notes) orientation and edge roles; see blueprints/templates/office-room-v2.yaml
This file is one standalone office room; not a placed room. It carries no
coordinates and no fort-specific anchor; a caller supplies the anchor when
applying it.
Grid orientation; 5 columns by 5 rows; row 1 is the top (north) edge as
displayed below:
- the outer ring (rows 1 and 5, columns 1 and 5): this room's own wall;
nothing tiles against it.
- row 5; column 3: the entrance gap; open floor; no wall; no door.
- rows 2-4; columns 2-4: the 3x3 interior; the chair sits in its centre.
Every s cell is a finished-wall intent; not a material. This concrete file
resolves that intent as smooth (s; #dig mode) because it assumes the ring is
standing natural rock, the common case for a room carved into solid stone.
Where a ring tile is soil or not standing rock, smoothing cannot apply; a
standing wall of soil cannot be finished by one blueprint (dig it out, wait,
then place a constructed wall). See blueprints/README.md; Resolving the wall
intent. The verb reports such tiles rather than leaving them rough.
Phase order matters: dig and smooth the ring (shell), then smooth the interior
floor (floor), then place furniture and the zone (finish). Furniture blocks
smoothing, so the floor phase must be applied only after the interior is dug
and before the chair is built. v1 lacked the floor phase; its floor stayed rough.
Access to the room (a stair or corridor to the entrance gap) is a separate
concern; this template is the room only.
